summary: A feature story about Eric Thompson, a 42-year-old financial analyst from Willow Creek who rediscovered painting after finding old watercolors in his attic in September 2023. He practiced at home, took workshops and online courses, found community at an art fair, and exhibited his work in March 2024. Painting became a daily escape that also improved his professional life, with emotional fulfillment valued above sales.
one_line: Financial analyst Eric Thompson takes up painting again at 42, finding community, daily joy, and a first exhibition in 2024.
key_facts: Eric Thompson is a 42-year-old financial analyst from the suburb of Willow Creek.
On September 15, 2023, Eric found a forgotten set of watercolor paints while cleaning his attic; they dated from his college days.
Eric set up a makeshift studio in a corner of his living room and practiced every evening, starting with simple doodles.
He attended local art workshops and online courses to learn techniques, light and shadow, and texture.
On October 22, 2023, Eric attended his first local art fair and found a supportive community there.
At the art fair he met Marissa Johnson, a 60-year-old abstract painter who began painting in her late 50s.
Eric's friend Alice Turner, a graphic designer, introduced him to digital painting.
Painting became a daily escape for Eric, with practice before work, during lunch breaks, and in the evenings.
Eric began incorporating artistic elements into his work presentations, and colleagues and superiors praised the visually engaging approach.
On March 17, 2024, Eric's paintings were featured in the local community center's biannual art display.
His artwork explores the interplay of daily life and nature and the subtleties of human emotion.
Eric's paintings began to sell, but financial gain was never his primary motivator.
